children: All passengers surveyed reported timeliness issues over the past 12 months, while 79 per cent faced problems with information and transparency
All SpiceJet passengers surveyed faced timeliness issues over the past 12 months, while nine in 10 reported problems with customer service, according to a survey report.

The report, based on 15,923 responses from SpiceJet passengers across more than 265 districts, found that 79 per cent of respondents had faced issues with information timeliness and transparency. Another 68 per cent each reported concerns over aircraft quality and maintenance and baggage handling.

The findings come as the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a show-cause notice to the airline over operational and regulatory concerns. The report found that complaints had increased across all eight parameters covered in the survey compared with the 2024 findings.
Customer Service Complaints Rise

Customer service recorded the steepest deterioration among the parameters tracked. The proportion of respondents reporting problems in this area increased from 15 per cent in 2024 to 90 per cent in 2026, a rise of 75 percentage points.

Complaints relating to staff attitude and courtesy rose from 15 per cent to 53 per cent over the same period. Issues with timeliness increased from 59 per cent to 100 per cent, while concerns about information timeliness and transparency climbed from 48 per cent to 79 per cent.

The report also found that 53 per cent of respondents had faced issues with food quality, compared with 26 per cent in 2024. Complaints about aircraft quality and maintenance increased from 33 per cent to 68 per cent, while those relating to baggage handling rose from 41 per cent to 68 per cent.

Issues with onboard entertainment systems were reported by 32 per cent of respondents, up from 15 per cent in 2024. Respondents could select more than one problem in the survey, so the percentages do not add up to 100.
Flight Disruptions Intensify

SpiceJet's operational difficulties have worsened in recent months, with cancellations and delays affecting passengers across several routes. The report stated that the airline's domestic market share fell to 0.6 per cent in September 2026 and remained at that level in October. It carried around 73,000 domestic passengers in September, compared with 5.92 lakh in January.
On 19 November, the airline cancelled 31 of the 42 flights scheduled at Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, while its on-time performance stood at 25 per cent.

The report also cited DGCA data showing that SpiceJet recorded an on-time performance of 16.6 per cent at the country's top 10 airports in September, the lowest among domestic carriers. Its cancellation rate stood at 20.29 per cent, against an industry average of 1.15 per cent.

The airline's operational constraints have also been reflected in its reduced fleet. The report said SpiceJet was operating around 10-15 flights daily, against approximately 66 flights cleared under the winter schedule.
DGCA Issues Show-Cause Notice

The DGCA issued a show-cause notice to SpiceJet on November 17, giving the airline seven days to respond. The notice flagged concerns over compliance with route dispersal guidelines, eligibility norms for international operations, deteriorating punctuality and failure to operate the approved schedule.

It also raised concerns over passenger facilitation during disruptions, an unpaid regulatory penalty, uncertainty over mandatory insurance renewal, delayed payments to overseas service providers and the grounding of a majority of the airline's fleet.

The regulator also noted that the airline had not submitted a credible plan for returning grounded aircraft to service, according to the report. Separately, the Ministry of Civil Aviation's AirSewa portal had recorded 7,674 grievances against SpiceJet as of 19 November 2026.
Passengers Seek Refunds, Updates
Passengers surveyed want the airline to stop selling tickets on flights it cannot operate and withdraw services that have remained grounded for several days.

They have also called for real-time communication on delays and cancellations, with revised departure information shared in advance. Respondents want refunds credited to the original payment method within the prescribed timelines and meals and accommodation provided during prolonged delays.
The report said its findings would be shared with the Ministry of Civil Aviation and the DGCA.
